components.name: Body shell
components.description: The painted outer shell that shapes the vehicle and protects the cabin.
components.purpose: Gives the vehicle its shape, manages airflow and carries the paint finish.
components.detail: Most modern cars use a unibody: the body and the main structure are a single welded shell rather than a body bolted onto a separate frame.

components.name: Hood
components.description: The hinged panel covering the engine bay.
components.purpose: Protects the engine bay and gives access for routine checks.
components.detail: Hoods are often designed to deform in a controlled way to help reduce injury to pedestrians in a collision.

components.name: Doors
components.description: Four hinged side doors with integrated windows.
components.purpose: Give access to the cabin and add side-impact protection.
components.detail: Doors usually contain a reinforcement beam, the window regulator, speakers and wiring, all hidden behind the inner trim panel.

components.name: Tailgate
components.description: The top-hinged rear door of the cargo area.
components.purpose: Gives wide access to the cargo area.
components.detail: SUV tailgates are hinged at the roof so the opening reaches almost floor level, making loading easier.

components.name: Wheels and tyres
components.description: Four wheels with tyres, the only parts touching the road.
components.purpose: Support the vehicle's weight and transfer driving, braking and steering forces to the road.
components.detail: The tyre's contact patch with the road is roughly the size of a hand, so tyre pressure and tread condition matter a lot for grip.

components.name: Lights
components.description: Headlights at the front and tail lights at the rear.
components.purpose: Let the driver see and let other road users see the vehicle.
components.detail: Many vehicles use LED lighting because it is efficient, long-lasting and switches on instantly.

components.name: Glazing
components.description: Windshield, rear window and fixed side glass.
components.purpose: Provides visibility while keeping wind and weather out.
components.detail: Windshields are typically laminated glass: a plastic layer between two glass sheets holds fragments together if the glass breaks.

components.name: Engine
components.purpose: Converts the chemical energy in fuel into rotating mechanical energy.
components.detail: Inside each cylinder, a piston moves through four strokes — intake, compression, power and exhaust. The pistons turn a crankshaft, which delivers rotation to the transmission.

components.name: Transmission
components.description: A simplified gearbox mounted beside the engine.
components.purpose: Changes the ratio between engine speed and wheel speed.
components.detail: Low gears multiply torque for pulling away; high gears let the engine turn slowly at cruising speed. In a front-wheel-drive layout the gearbox and differential are combined into one unit called a transaxle.

components.name: Drive shafts
components.description: Two shafts linking the transmission to the front wheels.
components.purpose: Carry rotation from the transmission to the driven wheels.
components.detail: Constant-velocity (CV) joints at each end let the shafts keep turning smoothly while the wheels steer and the suspension moves.

components.name: Radiator
components.description: A heat exchanger at the front of the engine bay.
components.purpose: Removes excess heat from the engine coolant.
components.detail: Hot coolant flows through thin tubes while air passes over the fins between them, carrying heat away. A fan helps pull air through when the vehicle is moving slowly.

components.name: 12 V battery
components.description: A low-voltage battery in the engine bay.
components.purpose: Powers the starter motor and electrical systems when the engine is off.
components.detail: Once the engine runs, an alternator recharges the battery and supplies the electrical systems.

components.name: Exhaust system
components.description: Pipes, a catalytic converter and a silencer running under the car.
components.purpose: Carries exhaust gases away, reduces harmful emissions and noise.
components.detail: The catalytic converter uses precious-metal catalysts to convert pollutants such as carbon monoxide into less harmful gases. The silencer (muffler) reduces noise.

components.name: Front brake assembly
components.description: A simplified model of a disc brake assembly.
components.purpose: Slows the wheels by clamping pads against a spinning disc.
components.detail: Pressing the pedal pushes hydraulic fluid to the calipers, which squeeze friction pads against the brake discs. Friction turns the vehicle's motion into heat.

components.name: Rear brake assembly
components.description: Smaller disc brakes on the rear wheels.
components.purpose: Share braking effort and keep the vehicle stable while stopping.
components.detail: Rear brakes are usually smaller because weight shifts forward during braking, so the front wheels do most of the work.

components.name: Front suspension
components.description: Spring-and-damper struts at the front wheels.
components.purpose: Absorbs bumps and keeps the tyres in contact with the road.
components.detail: The coil spring supports the vehicle's weight; the damper (shock absorber) controls how quickly the spring moves so the car does not keep bouncing.

components.name: Rear suspension
components.description: Spring-and-damper units at the rear wheels.
components.purpose: Supports the rear of the vehicle and smooths the ride.
components.detail: Suspension design is a trade-off between comfort, handling and load capacity.

components.name: Chassis rails
components.description: Longitudinal rails and cross-members under the floor.
components.purpose: Provide a stiff base that the suspension and powertrain attach to.
components.detail: In a unibody vehicle these rails are welded into the floor structure and also help absorb crash energy.

components.name: Fuel tank
components.description: A tank under the rear seats.
components.purpose: Stores fuel and feeds it to the engine through a pump.
components.detail: Placing the tank ahead of the rear axle, under the seats, keeps it away from the most crash-exposed areas.
